articleTitle: A message: a message from your division director
publicationTitle: IEEE Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing Newsletter
abstract: The IEEE is one of the largest professional societies in the world. Its 180,000 members from all over the world have a great variety of interests. The Board of Directors is charged with the responsibility of discerning the needs of the members and setting policies and priorities that result in activities that meet these needs. Because of the heterogeneous nature of the membership, the Board of Directors has been structured to give significant respresentation to specific interest groups. Ten of the members, called Regional Directors, represent geographical areas - six in the United States and four from the rest of the world. Seven members, called Division Directors, represent the Groups and Societies (G/Ss). The representation for the G/Ss is obtained by assigning each G/S to an entity called a Division. Each Division has approximately the same number of members, and the G/Ss within the Division generally have some commonality in technical interest. The ten Regional Directors and seven Division Directors constitute a majority of the 29-member Board. As Director of Division I, my assignment is to represent the following four Groups and Societies: Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing; Circuits and Systems; Control Systems; and Information Theory. The total membership of these G/Ss is nearly 25,000. I urge all members of the G/Ss in Division I to express their opinion whenever possible, and I strongly encourage the individual G/Ss to conduct their own opinion polls on issues that particularly concern them.

abstract: The following report is based on information provided by the IEEE TAB office as of February 16, 1978 on the financial status of our Society as of December 31, 1977. IEEE Headquarters acts as the bursar for our Society, as well as for all other Groups and Societies in the IEEE. The Society's income consists of membership fees, support from the IEEE, interest, sales of Transactions and conference proceedings, IEEE Press sales of books written for our Society, meeting profits, and other income. Expenses are incurred by the Transactions, the Newsletter, meetings, IEEE staff administration, IEEE Headquarters service to the AdCom, and AdCom external costs. Income for 1977 exceeded expenses by about $64,500; income for 1978 is epxected to again exceed expenses by a modest amount. Our capital surplus at the end of the calendar year 1977 was $129,700 (less outstanding loans of $8,000). This cash balance is equivalent to approximately 80% of our annual budget.

articleTitle: Appointment [to US National Academy of Engineering]
publicationTitle: IEEE Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing Newsletter
abstract: W.W. Lang recently was elected to the National Academy of Engineering. A past president of ASSPS, Bill was a founder of the Institute for Noise Control Engineering (INCE). He has also been active in the Acoustical Society, ANSI, and international standards committees. He is employed by IBM in Poughkeepsie, New York, USA.
